newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo port says in P&O deal only if profitable.
newsitem.headline: Colombo port says in P&O deal only if profitable.

text.p: Sri Lankan Ports and Shipping Minister Mohamed Ashraff said on Thursday the government will lease part of Colombo port to a consortium led by the Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co only if it is profitable.

"If everything goes well, we will hand it over to P&O next July," he told a labour union leaders planning to stage a strike at the port on Friday to protest against the deal. "If not there'll be no deal."
Two labour unions have said its members among the port's 16,000-strong work force will strike on Friday in protest against plans to lease the Queen Elizabeth Quay.

The Sri Lanka Ports Authority, which runs Colombo, south Asia's trans-shipment hub, is currently holding talks with P&O to turn Queen Elizabeth Quay into a new container terminal to expand capacity and later build a new port adjacent to the present one.

The project, estimated to cost up to $ billion and take 10 years to build, will see the development of the southern part of the port with at least another six deep-draft berths, for fifth and sixth generation ships, with a capacity of two million containers per year.
Ashraff urged the port workers not to go ahead with their strike and damage the port's reputation, saying any deal with P&O was six months away.
"I'm appealing to you not to take hasty decisions," he said.
The P&O deal was required to expand capacity to handle rising container volumes and retain Colombo's position as a hub port, he said.
The port, with a capacity of 1.6 million containers, was expected to handle 1.3 million containers this year, up from just over a million last year, he said.
